candidate.blueprint_topic: Infection-prevention practices during surgical wound care
candidate.educational_objective: Prevent postoperative wound contamination by performing hand hygiene before and after wound care and limiting unnecessary contact with the incision or dressing by visitors and caregivers.

options.A: I will clean my hands before and after caring for the wound, and I will ask family or visitors not to touch the incision or dressing unnecessarily.
options.B: Hand hygiene is needed only if the dressing is visibly soiled because a closed surgical incision cannot become contaminated.
options.C: Family members can touch the incision or dressing without cleaning their hands as long as they do not have a fever.
options.D: I should avoid asking healthcare workers to clean their hands before wound care because gloves make hand hygiene unnecessary.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. CDC surgical-site-infection guidance instructs patients to clean their hands before and after caring for a surgical wound and advises that family and friends should not touch the wound or dressings unnecessarily. CDC hand-hygiene guidance also identifies wound-dressing changes as a specific time when hand cleaning is indicated. B is incorrect because hand hygiene is required around wound care even when visible soil is absent. C creates avoidable contamination risk and ignores hand-hygiene recommendations. D is incorrect because gloves do not replace hand hygiene; CDC guidance requires hand cleaning at appropriate points before and after patient or wound contact. The final item is intentionally distinct from V2-Q1863: Q1863 tests recognition of infection findings, whereas this item tests prevention of contamination during wound care.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current CDC sources directly support hand hygiene before and after wound care, limiting unnecessary visitor contact with surgical wounds/dressings, and the principle that glove use does not eliminate indicated hand hygiene.
candidate.source_document_title: Surgical Site Infection Basics; About Hand Hygiene for Patients in Healthcare Settings; CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices
candidate.source_locator: CDC 'Surgical Site Infection Basics' → After surgery: family/friends should not touch the surgical wound or dressings; always clean hands before and after caring for the wound; ask healthcare providers to clean their hands. CDC 'About Hand Hygiene for Patients in Healthcare Settings' → When patients and visitors should clean their hands: before and after changing wound dressings or bandages. CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices → Hand Hygiene: perform hand hygiene before aseptic tasks, after patient/environment contact and after glove removal.
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.source_version_date: CDC SSI Basics updated 2024-04-11; current CDC hand-hygiene and core-practice resources accessed 2026-08-18
